title: Running Edge0-145B for Frontier AI on Local Hardware
summary: Understanding what is edge0-145b allows developers to assess if this architecture meets their requirements for private, high-performance data processing.
body_markdown:
## Common questions about edge0-145b?


### Can Edge0-145B be fine-tuned on private data?


Within your own infrastructure, Edge0-145B supports full parameter fine-tuning and Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA). Your proprietary datasets never leave your controlled environment.


Because the model weights are hosted on your hardware, you can refine the model on internal documentation or specialized codebases without the risk of data leakage inherent in cloud-based fine-tuning services.


This local training capability ensures that the resulting specialized model remains a private intellectual property asset.


### Does Edge0-145B support image or audio input?


Designed for high-end reasoning and complex instruction following, Edge0-145B is a text-only LLM. It doesn't natively process multimodal inputs like images or audio files.


If your workflow requires visual or auditory processing, you must use a dedicated multimodal model to convert those inputs into text descriptions before passing them to Edge0-145B.


This separation of concerns ensures that the 145B parameter budget is dedicated entirely to language logic and reasoning accuracy.


### How does local execution guarantee 100% privacy?


The total absence of external network calls during the inference lifecycle guarantees privacy. No data packets can be intercepted or logged by a third-party provider.


When you run Edge0-145B locally, the input tokens, intermediate activations, and output strings exist only in your system's RAM and VRAM. This physical isolation eliminates the "man-in-the-middle" risk and ensures that sensitive queries aren't stored in a provider’s training loop or feedback logs.
